summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and diastolic heart failure, was admitted for abdominal pain and shortness of breath. Imaging revealed colitis likely due to ischemia and new pleural effusions from acute on chronic heart failure, exacerbated by recent discontinuation of torsemide and dietary salt intake. He was treated with IV diuresis, restarted on torsemide, and managed for recurrent C. difficile infection with oral vancomycin. A urine culture grew vancomycin-resistant enterococcus, and he developed mild healthcare-associated pneumonia, both treated with Augmentin. A colonoscopy showed aphthous ulcers consistent with ischemic colitis and radiation proctitis, with incidental polyps to be addressed later. His condition improved, and he was discharged home with a planned antibiotic taper, follow-up colonoscopy, and instructions to monitor weight and symptoms.
problems: Acute (reversible) ischemia of large intestine, extent unspecified
Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Enterocolitis due to Clostridium difficile, recurrent
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
